items.title: Conflict and crisis put six World Heritage sites at risk
items.summary: Armed conflict, insecurity and environmental pressures are threatening ancient cities, historic castles and one of the world's greatest wildlife migrations.

items.title: Cyberattacks and the digital divide are creating new barriers to HIV services
items.summary: Cyberattacks, data breaches, online harassment and other forms of technology-facilitated violence are becoming significant obstacles to HIV prevention and treatment, according to a UNAIDS specialist who says digital security has become inseparable from the fight against the epidemic itself.

items.title: Guterres: Fast-tracking West Bank outposts is a ‘flagrant violation’ of international law
items.summary: The United Nations continues to monitor developments in the Occupied Palestinian Territory amid rising violence and greater restrictions in the occupied West Bank.

items.title: High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution
items.summary: The AIDS epidemic could stage a comeback amid unequal access to breakthrough prevention medicines and a sharp decline in global funding, according to a UN report released on Monday ahead of the opening of the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

items.title: Lebanon: Israeli strikes ‘could amount to international crimes,’ warns Türk
items.summary: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk expressed concern about ongoing displacement and destruction caused by Israeli strikes against Lebanon as he concluded a two-day visit to the country on Monday.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Briefing on Ukraine as deadly Russian strikes hit cities and ports
items.summary: The UN Security Council met on Monday at Ukraine’s request, following recent large-scale Russian attacks on Kyiv and elsewhere. At least one civilian was killed and more than a dozen wounded in an overnight strike on the capital on 19 July that also damaged homes and civilian infrastructure. Ukrainian authorities described it as one of the largest and most intense attacks since the invasion began. Follow live updates below.

items.title: After war took her leg, this Ukrainian gymnast refused to give up
items.summary: When 10-year-old Ukrainian gymnast Sasha Paskal stepped onto the stage in New York's Times Square this week, she carried a message far bigger than her performance.

items.title: Gaza: Dialysis patients face gruelling hospital journey by donkey cart
items.summary: Shortly before sunrise, Palestinian Fathi Hajji begins an arduous thrice-weekly journey to Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis in the war-ravaged Gaza Strip.

items.title: Syria’s hopes for renewal hinge on rebuilding trust, lives and livelihoods
items.summary: A country long known as a meeting point of civilizations, Syria stands once again at a crossroads.

items.title: ‘I am somebody’: Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN
items.summary: When Samantha Richards and Angela Hifume walked into the Hall of Flags at United Nations Headquarters last week, they carried more than a folder of paper. They carried the voices of hundreds of street-connected children who had never expected anyone to listen.

items.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
items.summary: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country.

items.title: ‘Judges should be superhuman’: The invisible burden behind the bench
items.summary: When conflict erupts, disasters strike or political crises unfold, courts are among the few institutions expected to keep functioning – ensuring the essential rule of law is maintained.

items.title: ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes
items.summary: One month after twin earthquakes rocked Venezuela, thousands of women and girls continue to face difficulty in accessing essential healthcare and protection services, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday.

items.title: After an Ebola centre was attacked, peacekeepers moved in next door
items.summary: A new mobile UN peacekeeping base in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has allowed local authorities to continue responding to the fast-moving Ebola outbreak there after violence disrupted the work of medics at a treatment centre set up to contain the spread.

items.title: In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water
items.summary: In El Obeid, women and girls now face an impossible choice over something as basic as a bucket of water: risk a drone strike by collecting it in daylight, or risk rape by waiting until dark.

items.title: International Criminal Court Prosecutor Karim Khan dismissed
items.summary: Member States of the International Criminal Court dismissed its Prosecutor Karim Khan following disciplinary proceedings related to widely reported sexual misconduct allegations at an emergency session at UN Headquarters in New York on Friday.

items.title: Middle East: UN warns against wider escalation after Houthi attacks in the Red Sea
items.summary: As fighting intensifies in the Middle East, the United Nations on Friday warned against further escalation in the US-Iran war and the risks to global shipping amid the fight over control of the Strait of Hormuz.
